notes.md: - **Twenty Point Programme:** launched by the Government of India in **1975**, during the Emergency; restructured in **1982, 1986 and 2006** (TPP-2006, in force from 1 April 2007); monitored by the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation**.

new.s: About what share of GSDP is the Net Borrowing Ceiling that the Centre fixes for States under Article 293?
new.x: The Centre fixes a Net Borrowing Ceiling for States under Article 293 at about 3% of GSDP.
new.angle: U0325 notes gap: Net Borrowing Ceiling -> about 3% of GSDP

new.s: By when is the Polavaram project, a national project under Section 90 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, to be dedicated to the nation?
new.x: Polavaram was 89% complete in June 2026 and is to be dedicated by March 2027.
new.angle: U0325 notes gap: Polavaram -> completion target March 2027

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a unitary feature of the Indian Constitution?
o: Division of powers between the Union and the States
new.x: Single citizenship, an integrated judiciary, All India Services and emergency powers are unitary features; division of powers is a federal feature.
new.angle: U0325 notes gap: unitary features -> single citizenship, integrated judiciary, emergency powers

new.s: By what majority must each House of Parliament approve a proclamation of President's Rule?
o: Two-thirds of members present and voting
new.x: President's Rule, like a Financial Emergency, is approved by a simple majority; only a National Emergency needs a special majority.
new.angle: U0326 notes gap: President's Rule approval -> simple majority

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A proclamation of President's Rule must be approved by a special majority in each House of Parliament.
2. A proclamation of Financial Emergency is approved by a simple majority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both President's Rule and Financial Emergency need only a simple majority; a special majority is needed only for a National Emergency.
new.angle: U0326 notes gap: majority for approval of emergencies (352 special, 356/360 simple)

new.s: On which ground can the President proclaim a Financial Emergency under Article 360?
o: Failure of constitutional machinery in a State
Threat to the financial stability or credit of India
Failure of a State to comply with Union directions
new.x: Article 360 applies when the financial stability or credit of India or any part of it is threatened.
new.angle: U0326 notes gap: Financial Emergency -> ground (financial stability or credit)

new.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Article)          List-II (Ground)
A. Article 352            1. Failure of a State to comply with Union directions
B. Article 356            2. Threat to financial stability or credit
C. Article 360            3. War, external aggression or armed rebellion
D. Article 365            4. Failure of constitutional machinery in a State
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
new.x: Art. 352 – war, external aggression or armed rebellion; Art. 356 – failure of constitutional machinery; Art. 360 – financial stability or credit; Art. 365 – non-compliance with Union directions.
new.angle: U0326 notes gap: grounds of the three emergencies and Art 365 (match)

new.s: Which Constitutional Amendment Act is called the 'Mini-Constitution'?
new.x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) made such wide changes, including raising Lok Sabha and Assembly terms to 6 years, that it is called the 'Mini-Constitution'.
new.angle: U0326 notes gap: 42nd CAA -> 'Mini-Constitution'

new.s: With which case is the Allahabad High Court's setting aside of Indira Gandhi's 1971 election, the background to the 1975 Emergency, associated?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala
Minerva Mills v Union of India
Indira Nehru Gandhi v Raj Narain
new.x: The Allahabad High Court cancelled Indira Gandhi's 1971 election in the Raj Narain case (Indira Nehru Gandhi v Raj Narain), which led to the June 1975 Emergency.
new.angle: U0326 notes gap: 1975 Emergency background -> Indira Nehru Gandhi v Raj Narain

new.s: After Manipur, which State has been placed under President's Rule the most times?
new.x: Manipur has had President's Rule 11 times, the highest, followed by Uttar Pradesh with 10.
new.angle: U0326 #2 PR count by state -> Uttar Pradesh (10) after Manipur

new.s:
Consider the following statements about President's Rule:
1. The President can revoke it at any time.
2. Its revocation needs the approval of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: President's Rule can be revoked by the President at any time; no parliamentary approval is needed for revocation.
new.angle: U0326 notes gap: revocation of President's Rule -> no parliamentary approval

new.s: Which Ministry of the Government of India monitors the Twenty Point Programme, first launched in 1975?
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
new.x: The Twenty Point Programme, launched in 1975 and now called TPP-2006, is monitored by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
new.angle: U0326 web: PYQ y5121b07fc33 20-point programme -> monitoring ministry

new.s: In which of the following years was the Twenty Point Programme NOT restructured?
new.x: The Twenty Point Programme of 1975 was restructured in 1982, 1986 and 2006 (TPP-2006, in force from 1 April 2007).
new.angle: U0326 web: PYQ y5121b07fc33 20-point programme -> restructuring years

new.s: In which year was the Inter-State Council set up by a Presidential order under Article 263?
new.x: The Inter-State Council was set up by a Presidential order of 28 May 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's advice.
new.angle: U0327 notes gap: Inter-State Council -> set up 28 May 1990

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Inter-State Council:
1. It was set up by a Presidential order of 28 May 1990.
2. Its meetings are held in camera and it decides questions by consensus.
3. It has met at least three times every year since 1990.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The ISC (1990) meets in camera and decides by consensus; it is meant to meet at least three times a year but has met only about 11 times since 1990.
new.angle: U0327 notes gap: ISC -> meetings (3 a year required, only ~11 held)

new.s: Which of the following bodies, besides the Sarkaria Commission, had earlier backed an Inter-State Council under Article 263?
o: Administrative Reforms Commission and Rajamannar Committee
Kurian Joseph Committee and Punchhi Commission
new.x: Before Sarkaria, the ARC (1966-69) and the Rajamannar Committee (1969) had backed an Inter-State Council.
new.angle: U0327 notes gap: ISC -> earlier backers ARC and Rajamannar

new.s: Which of the following States was NOT a party to the Narmada Water Disputes Tribunal set up in 1969?
new.x: The Narmada tribunal (1969) involved Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.
new.angle: U0327 notes gap: Narmada tribunal -> States

new.s: Which of the following groups of water disputes tribunals involve Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Andhra Pradesh is a party to the Godavari, Krishna (I and II) and Vansadhara tribunals.
new.angle: U0327 notes gap: tribunals involving AP

new.s: In which year did the Centre set the terms of reference for KWDT-II on the Krishna water dispute between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
new.x: The Centre set the terms of reference for KWDT-II on the AP-Telangana dispute in October 2023.
new.angle: U0327 #8 KWDT-II -> AP-Telangana terms of reference 2023

new.s: For which projects did Telangana plan to seek national project status at the 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting (August 2026)?
new.x: At the 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting (Tamil Nadu, 20 Aug 2026), Telangana was to seek national status for Kaleshwaram and Palamuru-Rangareddy.
new.angle: U0327 #2 Southern Zonal Council meetings -> Telangana's national-status demand

new.s: To what share did the 14th Finance Commission raise the States' share in the divisible pool of central taxes?
new.x: The 14th Finance Commission raised devolution to 42% and made no distinction between special and general category States.
new.angle: U0328 #9 14th FC -> 42% devolution

new.s: How many recommendations did the Punchhi Commission on Centre-State relations make?
new.x: The Punchhi Commission (2007, report 2010) made 273 recommendations; Sarkaria made 247.
new.angle: U0328 notes gap: Punchhi Commission -> 273 recommendations

new.s: In which year did the Punchhi Commission submit its report?
new.x: The Punchhi Commission was appointed on 27 April 2007 and reported on 30 March 2010.
new.angle: U0328 #1 Commissions -> Punchhi report year 2010

new.s: Under which Prime Minister's government was the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution set up in February 2000?
new.x: The NCRWC under M.N. Venkatachaliah was set up by the Vajpayee government on 22 February 2000 and reported in 2002.
new.angle: U0328 #1 Commissions -> appointing government (NCRWC, Vajpayee)

new.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Article)          List-II (State)
A. Article 371A           1. Assam
B. Article 371B           2. Manipur
C. Article 371C           3. Nagaland
D. Article 371            4. Maharashtra and Gujarat
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
new.x: Art. 371 – Maharashtra and Gujarat; 371A – Nagaland; 371B – Assam; 371C – Manipur.
new.angle: U0328 #15 Article 371 provisions -> States

new.s: After which event was the NIA Act, 2008 enacted?
new.x: The National Investigation Agency Act was passed in 2008 after the 26/11 Mumbai attacks.
new.angle: U0328 notes gap: NIA Act 2008 -> after 26/11

new.s: Which of the following States had withdrawn general consent to the CBI, according to a Lok Sabha reply of December 2023?
new.x: The Dec 2023 Lok Sabha list of States that withdrew general consent included Telangana, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Punjab and others; Gujarat, Odisha and AP were not on it.
new.angle: U0328 #6 CBI general consent withdrawal -> States

new.s: Over how many subjects does the Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority (2026) give eastern Nagaland autonomy?
new.x: The FNTA gives eastern Nagaland autonomy over 46 subjects without affecting Article 371A.
new.angle: U0328 notes gap: FNTA -> 46 subjects

new.s: Ladakh was offered Article 371 safeguards (2026) instead of which constitutional provision it had demanded?
new.x: Ladakh was offered Article 371-type safeguards instead of inclusion in the Sixth Schedule.
new.angle: U0328 #15 Article 371 provisions -> Ladakh offer

new.s: Whose 1967 view, that the Union need not control health and education, did the Rajamannar Committee take forward?
new.x: The Rajamannar Committee took forward C.N. Annadurai's 1967 view that the Union need not control health and education.
new.angle: U0329 notes gap: Annadurai's 1967 view

new.s: How many recommendations did the Sarkaria Commission make in its report of 1988?
new.x: The Sarkaria Commission's report (January 1988) made 247 recommendations, of which 180 were accepted or implemented.
new.angle: U0330 #1/#8 Sarkaria report -> 247 recommendations
